::: {#exr-prac-gauss-iid-lik}
#### Gaussian log-likelihood (adapted from @kleinbaum2014applied, Chapter 5)

Let $\dsn{X} \siid \Normal(\mean, \varpar)$.

**(a)** Write the likelihood $\Lik(\mean, \varpar; \vx)$
for the observed data $\vx = (\dsn{x})$.

**(b)** Write the log-likelihood $\llik(\mean, \varpar; \vx)$.
Show that it can be written as

$$
\llik(\mean, \varpar; \vx)
= -\frac{n}{2}\logf{2\pi\varpar}
  - \frac{1}{2\varpar}\sumin (x_i - \mean)^2.
$$

**(c)** Derive the MLE $\hmean_{ML}$ and $\hvarpar_{ML}$.
:::

:::{#sol-prac-gauss-iid-lik}

**(a)**

$$
\ba
\Lik(\mean, \varpar; \vx)
&= \prodin (2\pi\varpar)^{-1/2}
  \expf{-\frac{(x_i - \mean)^2}{2\varpar}}
&& \text{(likelihood of an $\iid$ sample)}
\\
&= \paren{\prodin (2\pi\varpar)^{-1/2}}
  \paren{\prodin \expf{-\frac{(x_i - \mean)^2}{2\varpar}}}
&& \text{(regroup the factors of the product)}
\\
&= (2\pi\varpar)^{-n/2}
  \prodin \expf{-\frac{(x_i - \mean)^2}{2\varpar}}
&& \text{(product of $n$ copies of a power)}
\\
&= (2\pi\varpar)^{-n/2}
  \expf{\sumin -\frac{(x_i - \mean)^2}{2\varpar}}
&& \text{(product of exponentials)}
\\
&= (2\pi\varpar)^{-n/2}
  \expf{-\frac{1}{2\varpar}\sumin (x_i-\mean)^2}
&& \text{(factor the constant out of the sum)}
\ea
$$

**(b)**

$$
\ba
\llik(\mean, \varpar; \vx)
&= \logf{\Lik(\mean, \varpar; \vx)}
&& \text{(definition of the log-likelihood)}
\\
&= \logf{(2\pi\varpar)^{-n/2}
  \expf{-\frac{1}{2\varpar}\sumin (x_i-\mean)^2}}
&& \text{(likelihood from (a))}
\\
&= \logf{(2\pi\varpar)^{-n/2}}
  + \logf{\expf{-\frac{1}{2\varpar}\sumin (x_i-\mean)^2}}
&& \text{(log of a product)}
\\
&= -\frac{n}{2}\logf{2\pi\varpar}
  + \logf{\expf{-\frac{1}{2\varpar}\sumin (x_i-\mean)^2}}
&& \text{(log of a power)}
\\
&= -\frac{n}{2}\logf{2\pi\varpar}
   - \frac{1}{2\varpar}\sumin (x_i - \mean)^2
&& \text{($\logt$ undoes $\expt$)}
\ea
$$

**(c)**

**Deriving $\hmean_{ML}$:**

$$
\ba
\deriv{\mean}\llik
&= \deriv{\mean}\sb{-\frac{n}{2}\logf{2\pi\varpar}
   - \frac{1}{2\varpar}\sumin (x_i - \mean)^2}
&& \text{(log-likelihood from (b))}
\\
&= \deriv{\mean}\sb{-\frac{n}{2}\logf{2\pi\varpar}}
   + \deriv{\mean}\sb{-\frac{1}{2\varpar}\sumin (x_i - \mean)^2}
&& \text{(linearity of differentiation)}
\\
&= 0 + \deriv{\mean}\sb{-\frac{1}{2\varpar}\sumin (x_i - \mean)^2}
&& \text{(derivative of a constant)}
\\
&= \deriv{\mean}\sb{-\frac{1}{2\varpar}\sumin (x_i - \mean)^2}
&& \text{(drop the zero term)}
\\
&= -\frac{1}{2\varpar}\deriv{\mean}\sumin (x_i - \mean)^2
&& \text{(constant multiple rule)}
\\
&= -\frac{1}{2\varpar}\sumin \deriv{\mean}(x_i - \mean)^2
&& \text{(derivative of a sum is the sum of derivatives)}
\\
&= -\frac{1}{2\varpar}\sumin 2(x_i - \mean)\deriv{\mean}(x_i - \mean)
&& \text{(chain rule, outer function $u^2$)}
\ea
$$

The inner derivative is:

$$
\ba
\deriv{\mean}(x_i - \mean)
&= \deriv{\mean} x_i - \deriv{\mean} \mean
&& \text{(linearity of differentiation)}
\\
&= 0 - \deriv{\mean} \mean
&& \text{($x_i$ does not depend on $\mean$)}
\\
&= 0 - 1
&& \text{(derivative of $\mean$ with respect to itself)}
\\
&= -1
&& \text{(subtract)}
\ea
$$

Substituting the inner derivative back in:

$$
\ba
\deriv{\mean}\llik
&= -\frac{1}{2\varpar}\sumin 2(x_i - \mean) \cdot (-1)
&& \text{(inner derivative is $-1$)}
\\
&= -\frac{1}{2\varpar}\sumin -2(x_i - \mean)
&& \text{(multiply)}
\\
&= -\frac{1}{2\varpar} \cdot (-2) \sumin (x_i - \mean)
&& \text{(factor the constant $-2$ out of the sum)}
\\
&= \frac{1}{\varpar}\sumin (x_i - \mean)
&& \text{(multiply the constants)}
\\
&= \frac{1}{\varpar}\paren{\sumin x_i - \sumin \mean}
&& \text{(split the sum)}
\\
&= \frac{1}{\varpar}\paren{\sumin x_i - n\mean}
&& \text{(sum of $n$ copies of $\mean$)}
\ea
$$

Setting this to zero: $\hmean_{ML} = \bar{x} \eqdef \avgin x_i$.

**Deriving $\hvarpar_{ML}$:**

$$
\ba
\deriv{\varpar}\llik
&= \deriv{\varpar}\sb{-\frac{n}{2}\logf{2\pi\varpar}
   - \frac{1}{2\varpar}\sumin (x_i - \mean)^2}
&& \text{(log-likelihood from (b))}
\\
&= \deriv{\varpar}\sb{-\frac{n}{2}\paren{\logf{2\pi} + \logf{\varpar}}
   - \frac{1}{2\varpar}\sumin (x_i - \mean)^2}
&& \text{(log of a product)}
\\
&= \deriv{\varpar}\sb{-\frac{n}{2}\logf{2\pi} - \frac{n}{2}\logf{\varpar}
   - \frac{1}{2\varpar}\sumin (x_i - \mean)^2}
&& \text{(distribute $-\tfrac{n}{2}$)}
\\
&= \deriv{\varpar}\sb{-\frac{n}{2}\logf{2\pi} - \frac{n}{2}\logf{\varpar}
   - \frac{1}{2}(\varpar)^{-1}\sumin (x_i - \mean)^2}
&& \text{(write $\tfrac{1}{2\varpar}$ as $\tfrac{1}{2}(\varpar)^{-1}$)}
\\
&= \deriv{\varpar}\sb{-\frac{n}{2}\logf{2\pi}}
   + \deriv{\varpar}\sb{-\frac{n}{2}\logf{\varpar}}
   + \deriv{\varpar}\sb{-\frac{1}{2}(\varpar)^{-1}\sumin (x_i - \mean)^2}
&& \text{(linearity of differentiation)}
\\
&= 0 + \deriv{\varpar}\sb{-\frac{n}{2}\logf{\varpar}}
   + \deriv{\varpar}\sb{-\frac{1}{2}(\varpar)^{-1}\sumin (x_i - \mean)^2}
&& \text{(derivative of a constant)}
\\
&= \deriv{\varpar}\sb{-\frac{n}{2}\logf{\varpar}}
   + \deriv{\varpar}\sb{-\frac{1}{2}(\varpar)^{-1}\sumin (x_i - \mean)^2}
&& \text{(drop the zero term)}
\\
&= \deriv{\varpar}\sb{-\frac{n}{2}\logf{\varpar}}
   + \deriv{\varpar}\sb{-\frac{1}{2}\sumin (x_i - \mean)^2 (\varpar)^{-1}}
&& \text{(reorder the factors)}
\\
&= -\frac{n}{2}\deriv{\varpar}\logf{\varpar}
   - \frac{1}{2}\sumin (x_i - \mean)^2 \deriv{\varpar}(\varpar)^{-1}
&& \text{(constant multiple rule)}
\\
&= -\frac{n}{2}(\varpar)^{-1}
   - \frac{1}{2}\sumin (x_i - \mean)^2 \deriv{\varpar}(\varpar)^{-1}
&& \text{(derivative of $\log$)}
\\
&= -\frac{n}{2}(\varpar)^{-1}
   - \frac{1}{2}\sumin (x_i - \mean)^2 \paren{-(\varpar)^{-2}}
&& \text{(power rule)}
\\
&= -\frac{n}{2}(\varpar)^{-1}
   + \frac{1}{2}\sumin (x_i - \mean)^2 (\varpar)^{-2}
&& \text{(multiply)}
\\
&= -\frac{n}{2}(\varpar)^{-1}
   + \frac{1}{2}(\varpar)^{-2}\sumin (x_i - \mean)^2
&& \text{(reorder the factors)}
\ea
$$

Setting this to zero and solving:

$$
\ba
0
&= -\frac{n}{2}(\varpar)^{-1} + \frac{1}{2}(\varpar)^{-2}\sumin (x_i - \mean)^2
&& \text{(set the derivative to zero)}
\\
\frac{n}{2}(\varpar)^{-1}
&= \frac{1}{2}(\varpar)^{-2}\sumin (x_i - \mean)^2
&& \text{(add $\tfrac{n}{2}(\varpar)^{-1}$ to both sides)}
\\
n(\varpar)^{-1}(\varpar)^2
&= (\varpar)^{-2}(\varpar)^2\sumin (x_i - \mean)^2
&& \text{(multiply both sides by $2(\varpar)^2$)}
\\
n\varpar
&= (\varpar)^{-2}(\varpar)^2\sumin (x_i - \mean)^2
&& \text{($(\varpar)^{-1}(\varpar)^2 = \varpar$)}
\\
n\varpar
&= \sumin (x_i - \mean)^2
&& \text{($(\varpar)^{-2}(\varpar)^2 = 1$)}
\\
\varpar
&= \avgin (x_i - \mean)^2
&& \text{(divide both sides by $n$)}
\ea
$$

Substituting $\hmean_{ML} = \bar{x}$:

$$
\hvarpar_{ML} = \avgin (x_i - \bar{x})^2
$$

Note: this maximum likelihood estimator is a biased estimator of $\varpar$;
the unbiased sample variance divides by $n-1$.

:::
